TOP: Optimizely breach spreads malware across 178 organizations
WPPConnect releases steal secrets via trusted pipeline
Windows adds tighter controls for AI agents

P.h: Optimizely breach turns major websites into malware dispensers
P.p: TLDR IT reports attackers exploited Optimizely's experimentation software to push malicious JavaScript through sites of at least 178 organizations. The payloads went after cryptocurrency wallets and payment details.
P.s: Optimizely says it patched the vulnerability, removed injected code and revoked tokens. If you embed third-party scripts, review what they can load and watch for unexpected JavaScript on checkout pages.

items.h: WPPConnect releases steal secrets and WhatsApp sessions
items.d: TLDR InfoSec: unreviewed commits via a maintainer account shipped a module that sent env vars, .env files and session tokens to a Telegram bot. It had valid SLSA provenance and runs on import, so --ignore-scripts does not help.

items.h: Java4Shell: critical OpenJDK Base64 decoder RCE, CVSS 9.2
items.d: A hand-written AVX-512 assembly path overflows memory when fed 64 A characters. Confluence, Jira, Artifactory, Keycloak and Elasticsearch are named as exposed.

items.h: Malicious ONNX model leaks host files through a parser flaw
items.d: The model behaves normally until a trigger word fires. Upgrade onnxruntime to v1.27.0 or later and audit downloaded models like untrusted code.

items.h: Infoblox confirms breach via SharePoint migration vendor
items.d: A source says sensitive customer data was taken. Infoblox says products, cloud services and build processes were not involved.

P.h: Windows adds tighter controls for AI agents
P.p: TLDR IT says Microsoft announced new Windows controls for AI agents: preview process containers, experimental hardware-isolated micro VMs, and generally available learning modes that let IT observe agent behavior before enforcing limits.
P.s: Teams also gains Impersonation Protection, a Facilitator agent skill that scans transcripts for deceptive requests, and a Defender data table for forensics. Intune previews automatic updates for self-installed apps.

items.h: Sign2Shell: five Brazilian signing extensions allow drive-by RCE
items.d: Each is rated CVSS 9.6. Websites can pick DLLs the native host loads, with no path or signature checks. Some chains need only a page visit or an ad iframe.

items.h: GitDoor and GraphDoor turn GitHub and SharePoint into covert C2
items.d: Operation ShadowCloud targets government bodies in Asia and Africa, using MeshCentral Agent and DLL sideloading.

items.h: BubbleLoader turns WinRAR and Firefox Launcher into droppers
items.d: Shellcode hides in a fake PNG, and padding is overwritten so the hash changes each run. Enforce code-signing checks.

items.h: Access Dental Management breach affects over 340,000
items.d: Attackers accessed the network May 1 to 4. Exposed data includes SSNs, medical records and insurance details.

P.h: Uber governs autonomous AI agents across their lifecycle
P.p: TLDR DevOps reports Uber built a framework that judges whether an agent's proposed action fits the user's request, purpose, permissions and context. It combines pre-deployment registration, runtime behavioral authorization and post-deployment replay.
P.s: Per-agent intents worked better than generic thresholds. Separately, Canonical gives Ubuntu Pro users early access to AI-generated security patches through an opt-in archive called Edge.

tiles.t: kube-proxy IPVS backend to be removed
tiles.d: Kubernetes plans removal in 2026 to cut maintenance for SIG Network.
Browser engine for AI agents on Workers, Apache 2.0, with CDP support for Puppeteer.
VPA tunes CPU and memory while HPA scales on proxy connections.
Memory-limiter placement, sampling trade-offs, trace-aware routing for tail sampling.
Partial network failure made runner assignment exhaust memory and restart.

items.h: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.d: Astra targets hard projects, Sol everyday tasks. Rolling out in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API with fewer output tokens.

items.h: Outages hit banks, air travel, NSA and Apple over four days
items.d: The DNI dismissed malicious causes. Researchers say AI speeds vulnerability discovery and patching strains uptime.

items.h: Claude Docs launch: 60 errors across 2 billion requests
items.d: Anthropic used a chaos loop and never rolled back. About 50 memory-optimized pods served it.

items.h: Copilot becomes the new OS for work
items.d: Word, Excel and PowerPoint inside Copilot are now generally available, says Nadella.
